summary: Focused re-test of the iteration_16 MEDIUM CSS bug — Marketplace 'Shop by Category' tile hero images. RESULT: Bug is NOT fixed. Images still render as narrow vertical strips (~19–32px wide × 150px tall) instead of filling the ~170px-wide tile. Height (150px) is now correct, but width:100% on .ct-img is not being honored because the parent .cat-tile is a <button> element (buttons apply a special inline shrink-to-fit content flow that ignores width:100% on child spans, even when those spans are display:flex). Regression checks all pass: stories-reel present, curated shelves render 20+ real listing card images, horizontal overflow = 0px at 1440x900, no console errors.

ui_bugs.issue: Category tile hero images still collapsed to narrow vertical strips. Measured .ct-img bounding boxes at 1440x900 (logged in as owner): cat-tile-gear w=19.28px h=150px; cat-tile-vehicles w=32.28px h=150px; cat-tile-art w=30.28px h=150px; cat-tile-jobs w=21.30px h=150px. Expected width ~170px (full tile width). Labels appear beside the strip rather than below because the button's inline flow layout is not being broken by the current CSS. The width:100% + height:150px fix on .ct-img is insufficient — <button> element does not treat width:100% child spans the same way a <div> would. .cat-tile itself has no display/width set (App.css line 2369), so its inline-flex/inline-block children shrink to content width.

action_items: In /app/frontend/src/App.css around line 2369, update .cat-tile to be a proper block flex column so its span children can fill width. Recommended patch: `.cat-tile { background:none; border:none; cursor:pointer; text-align:center; text-decoration:none; display:flex; flex-direction:column; align-items:stretch; width:100%; padding:0; }`  — This forces the <button> out of its default inline shrink-to-fit content flow. Keep the existing .ct-img rule (width:100%; height:150px; display:flex; ...). After this, .ct-img will render at full tile width (~170px) and the label/count will stack below the hero image, matching the intended design.
critical_code_review_comments: Using <button> for cat-tile causes CSS layout surprises; consider either (a) forcing display:flex/flex-direction:column on the button, or (b) refactoring to a <div role='button'> wrapping the content. The <button> approach also implicitly makes the whole tile a form-submit target which can cause unintended submits inside forms.

The .ct-img fallback background gradient works, but .ct-ph is absolutely inline-sized (~20px) so the Jobs tile placeholder text 'Jobs' is barely visible inside the collapsed strip too — will be resolved by the same fix.
